description: Trading bot that decides buy/sell on a live price feed and executes real on-chain trades on Monad via Kuru's order book, one decision every ~300ms block.
how_used_jev: Jev answers a typed buy/sell question against the live price feed each block; the bot posts a real post-only limit order one tick inside the touch based on the answer.
author: @jarrodwatts

benchmark.notes: author reports ~81ms model latency; hot loop makes exactly two RPC round trips to fit the block budget

security_status.notes: executes real trades with real funds - high blast radius if Jev misjudges; good Watchdog-lens candidate once it's run longer

description: Open-source browser agent that found a real Google Flights result (Zurich to London) in 7.1s for $0.0039.
how_used_jev: Jev picks the next browser action (CLICK, TYPE_TEXT, SELECT, SCROLL, WAIT, DONE, BLOCKED) and target element index from the indexed DOM each step; a small LLM only runs when the action is TYPE_TEXT.
author: @gregpr07

benchmark.task: Zurich -> London flight search on real Google Flights

description: Rebuilt a Tesla Full Self-Driving-style decision loop with Jev in under an hour.
how_used_jev: Used Jev as the real-time decision primitive driving the control loop instead of an autoregressive LLM.
author: @jpschroeder

security_status.notes: safety-critical decision domain (driving) - no repo link yet to inspect failure handling

description: Ran ~5,000 Jev requests for about $2 total across classification, model routing, intent detection, and steering tasks.
how_used_jev: Used Jev as a general-purpose typed-decision layer across several distinct task types to test cost and behavior at volume.
author: @MichaelLee04

cost_signal.basis: ~5,000 requests for ~$2 total (~$0.0004/request) across classification, routing, intent, steering

description: Curated thread collecting the best Jev explanations and examples found on X. Not a build, but a useful index of other projects.
author: @moritzkremb

description: Desktop AI IDE that uses Jev to route work to the right coding bot instead of guessing, and to triage incoming noise on wakeup.
how_used_jev: Jev picks the correct bot or declines rather than guessing; in wakeup triage it drops noise batches and keeps mixed batches in ~318ms, with critical items always surviving and the system failing open if Jev fails.
author: @LazyIDE

replaces.notes: positions itself against paid AI IDEs (Cursor-style) but author hasn't made a direct replacement claim yet - needs follow-up before scoring

benchmark.task: wakeup triage - mixed noise/signal batch classification

security_status.notes: explicitly fails open (lets routing through) if Jev fails - worth a Watchdog-lens note on what 'fails open' means for a routing decision

description: Public Grok skill that pairs Grok with Browser Use's Jev Ultrafast agent for fast, cheap automated website checks.
how_used_jev: Wraps Browser Use's Jev-driven browser agent as a Grok skill so Grok can delegate page navigation/checks to Jev's fast typed-decision loop instead of a full LLM browsing pass.
author: @OmegaEdge

description: Security classifier for coding-agent tool calls, rebuilt on Jev instead of a chat model.
how_used_jev: Jev scores every tool call an agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini) makes, flagging prompt injection and scanning skills; author reports 3.4x faster and 28x cheaper than Haiku 4.5 for the same classifier.
author: @lbki34064963

replaces.notes: author's own claim, not independently verified: same classification job, 3.4x faster and 28x cheaper

cost_signal.basis: author reports 28x cheaper for the same tool-call classification task (unverified)

security_status.notes: this tool IS a security guardrail - prime Watchdog-lens candidate: has anyone tried to get a malicious tool call past jev-guard's injection detection?

description: Novelty npm library that checks whether a number is even by asking Jev.
how_used_jev: Sends the number to Jev as a typed yes/no question and returns its answer; a joke/demo package rather than production tooling.
author: @wobsoriano

description: Safety gate that stops autonomous coding agents from running dangerous raw bash commands.
how_used_jev: Combines hard-coded local rules with Jev semantic checks (intent, severity, exfiltration/curl-to-bash detection) to gate what Claude Code and Codex are allowed to execute.
author: @gpkmasa

security_status.notes: gates raw bash execution for coding agents - a false negative here means arbitrary code execution; strongest Watchdog-lens candidate in this batch

description: Open-source, Jev-compatible API that mimics Jev's fast parallel typed-decision behavior on an open model.
how_used_jev: Not Jev itself: runs Qwen3.6-35B-A3B behind an SGLang radix cache to approximate Jev's prefill reuse and parallel System One-style generation, benchmarked at 64 tasks in under 1 second.
author: @ekzhang1

replaces.notes: self-hosted approximation on an open model, not a drop-in - own accuracy/calibration unverified against Jev

benchmark.notes: uses SGLang radix cache for prefill reuse

description: CLI tool that gives any agent harness access to Jev-backed yes/no questions, multiple-choice selection, and criteria scoring.
how_used_jev: Wraps Jev's typed-decision API behind simple CLI commands (yes/no, choose between options, score against criteria) so any agent harness can call it.
author: @ctatedev

description: Pre-install security gate for npm packages that screens for malicious lifecycle scripts.
how_used_jev: Runs a ~100ms Jev check before an npm install using three typed primitives: Choice (intent), Score (severity), and Noul (exfiltration / curl-to-bash detection).
author: @GNUmanth

replaces.notes: candidate to compare against paid supply-chain scanners (e.g. Socket) - not yet researched

security_status.notes: exists specifically to catch malicious install scripts - a false negative here is exactly what the Watchdog lens should track

description: End-to-end verification that the GITHUB_SUBMIT_TOKEN wiring actually opens a PR. Safe to close without merging.
